newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power holds firm amid outages,weather.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power holds firm amid outages,weather.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. remained strong Wednesday in light trading, supported by gradually increasing air-conditioning demand and reduced generation, market sources said.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Thursday delivery was again pegged in the $25.00-26.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range for 16-hour blocks.
For eight-hour blocks, firm, peak power also traded near $26.00, some power marketers said.
Firm, off-peak power for next-day delivery at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally valued at $15.00-$16.00.
Hourly prices for electricity among Florida's utilities were assessed steady in the $29.00 to low-$30 range.
In the northwestern part of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory, firm, peak electricity for next-day delivery was assessed steady in the $18.00-$19.00 area.
TVA's 1,065 megawatt (MW) Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Decatur, Ala., has fully shut power production, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported earlier today.
The restart of the unit was not known. TVA's Browns Ferry 3 unit is operating at full power. The restart of TVA's 1,148 MW Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 was also still unknown.
TVA offered limited power this morning, but the continued shutdown of the unit and additional outages deterred TVA from offering any power later in the day, market sources said.
According to Weather Service Corp, Southeast temperatures are expected to turn gradually cooler this week, with five- to 10-degrees below-normal temperatures forecast for Saturday.
